content.title: What are List and ArrayList?
content.description: List is an interface in the Java Collections Framework that represents an ordered collection of elements. ArrayList is a resizable array implementation of the List interface that provides fast random access and dynamic storage.

content.content: Unlike arrays, which have a fixed size, an ArrayList grows and shrinks dynamically as elements are added or removed. Since ArrayList implements the List interface, it maintains insertion order, allows duplicate elements, and provides index-based access, making it one of the most commonly used collection classes in Java.

content.title: Why Use ArrayList?
content.content: ArrayList eliminates the need to manage array sizes manually and provides convenient methods for adding, removing, searching, and updating elements.
The List interface defines an ordered collection. Elements are stored according to insertion order, duplicate values are allowed, and every element has an index.

content.title: Key Idea
content.description: Program to the List interface while using ArrayList as the implementation. This makes your code more flexible.

content.title: Expandable Notebook
content.content: An ArrayList is like a notebook with expandable pages. You can easily add new pages, remove old ones, and access any page by its page number.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: ArrayList is one of the most frequently asked Java interview topics. Candidates should understand its internal dynamic array implementation, time complexity, common methods, and differences from arrays and LinkedList.

items.question: Can ArrayList store primitive data types directly?
items.answer: No. It stores objects. Primitive values are automatically wrapped using wrapper classes.

items.question: Does ArrayList have a fixed size?
items.answer: No. It automatically resizes when needed.

items.question: Should ArrayList always be used?
items.answer: No. Use LinkedList when frequent insertions and deletions are required.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: ArrayList provides dynamic storage, fast index-based access, maintains insertion order, and allows duplicate elements.
